az_scrap_metal.blurb: A small bouldering spot on South Mountain in Phoenix, set on a sandy rise just before the Mormon Trail meets the loop trail that branches from it. A boulder shaped a bit like a football is the landmark to look for. Six problems are on offer, running from V0 up to V3, with most of them on the gentler end, so it suits climbers building up rather than those after hard testpieces. It is a short outing from the trail, and the surrounding hillside is covered in boulders that are mostly too crumbly to climb.

az_promenade_wall.blurb: Promenade Wall is a compact sport wall inside the Colosseum sector of the Catalina Highway cliffs on Mount Lemmon, outside Tucson. It is really two short walls: one leans out a little and has a roomy ledge for belaying, and the other runs alongside the trail up to the cliff. Six routes, five of them bolted and one on gear, spread from 5.7 into the 5.11 range, with a cluster around 5.10. It works as a warm-up before harder neighbours, or as a relaxed day of moderate climbing when linked with the Aqueducts routes nearby.

az_red_bull_and_bananas_boulder.blurb: A single big overhanging boulder on South Mountain in Phoenix, sitting beneath a stretch of large dark slabs on the north side of a sandy wash. Six problems are packed onto it. Half sit around V1, a couple step up to V2 and V3, and one standout reaches V6, so there is something for a mixed group but the hard end is limited. Expect a short desert wash walk from the park trail to reach it, so it makes a good quick stop rather than a full day destination.

az_tyrannosaurus_rex.blurb: A bouldering area on South Mountain in Phoenix, built around one of the largest boulders in its wash. Six problems in all, and they lean hard: the spread runs from around V3 up through the V8 range to one at V10, so this is a stop for stronger boulderers rather than beginners. The big boulder offers steep, powerful lines with a clear landing, and a few other blocks sit behind it. Getting here means heading out from the trailhead toward the Desert Classic Trail.

az_moby_dick.blurb: A South Mountain bouldering area in Phoenix, found about midway up the hillside between two other boulder areas in the Equestrian section. Its six problems cover a wide range, from an easy V0 to a top-end V9, with a few mid-grade lines between them, so it has something for most levels without being large. The faces point toward the east and are out of the sun in the afternoon, which helps on warm days. Only a landmark description is available for finding it, so allow time to hunt around on the hill.

az_five_two_slab_area.blurb: A beginner-oriented bouldering patch on South Mountain in Phoenix, part of the Equestrian section. Six problems, all at the very bottom of the scale: four are easier than V0 and two sit around V0. Most are short slabs on or between ground-level blocks, plus a short corner that makes use of a ledge and a brief problem on a ledge with small toe holds. It is a gentle place for first-time boulderers or kids to learn movement, though it will not hold a strong climber's interest for long.

az_glade_wall.blurb: Glade Wall is a west-facing wall in Queen Creek Canyon near Superior, within the Faulty Towers section of Lower Devil's Canyon, with a small glade at its centre. Six routes, mostly trad with a single bolted line, range from 5.8 into the 5.11 range, with about half sitting at 5.9. The rock is rated as relatively good for the area, and the protection ranges from fully gear-protected to one sport route, making it a decent pick for a trad climber wanting moderate lines.
